diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same four equation hold if we replace $\va$ with $\matR_\va$, $\vy$ with $\matR_\vy$ and $\Mprod$ with matrix product.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof lists four properties of the constructed candidate \(\vy\) using the operation \(^\pinv\) (entrywise inverse for tubes / Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse for matrices) and claims these translate to the four Penrose equations establishing \(\matR_\vy\) as the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of \(\matR_\va\). However, the Moore–Penrose conditions require Hermiticity conditions \((AX)^*=AX\) and \((XA)^*=XA\), which correspond to the ring conjugation \(^\sconj\) (as in Lemma lem:added-2), not to \(^\pinv\). The proof verifies \((\matR_\va\matR_\vy)^+=\matR_\va\matR_\vy\) (self-pseudoinverse property) instead of \((\matR_\va\matR_\vy)^*=\matR_\va\matR_\vy\) (Hermitian property), so the claim that Moore–Penrose conditions are met is not established and the subsequent uniqueness argument is invalid.

failure_location.quote: Thus, $\matR_\vy$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\matR_\va$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Moore–Penrose uniqueness step with the correct argument: since both \(\vy\) and \(\va^\winv\) satisfy the two ring-theoretic Penrose equations \(a x a = a\) and \(x a x = x\) in the commutative algebra \(\{\matM^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\vw)\matM : \vw\in\C^n\}\cong\C^n\) (a commutative von Neumann regular ring), the Lombardi–Quitte uniqueness result (already cited in Lemma lem:added-2) gives \(\vy=\va^\winv\), and since \(\vy\) is real so is \(\va^\winv\).
issues.overall_effect: The proof that the weak inverse \(\vx^{\winv}=\matM^{-1}(\matM\vx)^{\pinv}\) is real (and hence belongs to \(\KM\)) is unproven as written. Lemma lem:added-2, which asserts \(\va^\winv\in\KM\) and the four Penrose-type properties of the weak inverse, relies on this lemma and is therefore unreliable.
issues.title: Invalid Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse argument in proof of realness of weak inverse
issues.why_classification: The fix replaces one uniqueness citation (Moore–Penrose) with another already-cited result (Lombardi–Quitte ring uniqueness) within the same proof structure. No new lemma, construction, or proof architecture is needed; the lemma's statement and all downstream guarantees are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since complex rows in $\matM$ come in pairs, the parity of the realness must be equal to the parity of $n$
The {\em realness} of $\KM$ or $\matM$ is the number of real rows in $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims there are \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) non-isomorphic tubal rings of size \(n\). However, the realness \(m\) must have the same parity as \(n\) and satisfy \(0\le m\le n\), giving \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) possible values (e.g., for \(n=2\): \(m\in\{0,2\}\), two values, but \(\lceil 2/2\rceil=1\); for \(n=4\): \(m\in\{0,2,4\}\), three values, but \(\lceil 4/2\rceil=2\)). By Proposition prop:added-3 each realness value yields a distinct canonical ring \(\mathbb{K}_{n,m}\cong\R^m\times\C^{(n-m)/2}\), so different realness values give non-isomorphic rings. The stated formula \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) is wrong for even \(n\); the correct count is \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\).

failure_location.quote: thus there are, up to isomorphism, $\lceil \nicefrac{n}{2} \rceil$ tubal rings

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) with \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) and note that different realness values give non-isomorphic rings (since \(\mathbb{K}_{n,m}\cong\R^m\times\C^{(n-m)/2}\) has a different number of \(\R\)-factors).
issues.overall_effect: The stated number of non-isomorphic tubal rings of size \(n\) is understated by one for every even \(n\). No formal results are affected.
issues.title: Wrong count of non-isomorphic tubal rings for even n
issues.why_classification: A local formula correction in a prose remark; no theorem, proof, or algorithm is affected and the correct count follows immediately from the parity constraint already stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we write $\va \Mleq \vb$ if $\matM(\vb - \va)$ is real and element-wise non-negative

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that for any two tubes, \(\va\Mgeq\vb\) implies \(\|\hat{\va}\|_F\ge\|\hat{\vb}\|_F\). This is false in general: \(\va\Mgeq\vb\) means \(\hat{\va}-\hat{\vb}\) is real and non-negative, but \(\hat{\vb}\) can have entries with large negative real parts. For example with \(n=1\), \(\hat{b}=-100\) and \(\hat{a}-\hat{b}=1\) gives \(\hat{a}=-99\), so \(|\hat{a}|^2=9801<10000=|\hat{b}|^2\) despite \(\va\Mgeq\vb\). The claim is valid when both \(\hat{\va}\) and \(\hat{\vb}\) are non-negative (as is the case for the singular tubes \(\hat{\vsigma}_j\)), which is the only case used to derive the monotonicity of \(\|\vsigma_i\|_F\).

failure_location.quote: Clearly, for any two tubes $\va$ and $\vb$ of the same size $\va \Mgeq \vb$ implies $\Fnorm{\hat{\va}} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vb}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to tubes whose transforms are non-negative: replace "for any two tubes" with "for any two tubes \(\va,\vb\) with \(\hat{\va},\hat{\vb}\ge 0\)" or state the inequality directly for the singular tubes \(\vsigma_i\), whose transforms satisfy \(\hat{\vsigma}_i\ge 0\).
issues.overall_effect: One proof step in Corollary cor:added-1 is invalid. However, the corollary's conclusions (\(\|\tenA\|_F^2=\sum_i\|\vsigma_i\|_F^2\) and \(\|\vsigma_1\|_F\ge\|\vsigma_2\|_F\ge\cdots\)) remain correct because the specific application is to singular tubes with non-negative transforms, for which the inequality holds.
issues.title: False general Frobenius-norm ordering claim in proof of Corollary cor:added-1
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short, local restriction of the claim to the non-negative case actually needed. The corollary and all downstream results (including the Eckart–Young theorems) retain their full statements and guarantees.
